summary: BUG-0093: retain CAP_SETUID in the installed nex-core-local service so its embedded Core agent can run the existing libvirt-qemu ISO-storage access probe. API impact: none; Core continues to self-register and report the existing storage-register record through Inventory.managed.

guide.reason: The documented automatic ISO storage registration workflow is unchanged; this restores its packaged execution.

api.reason: No Controller/Core or client-facing API operation, schema, authorization rule, or observed result changes; the existing managed inventory adoption path is reused.

roadmap.reason: This restores an existing implementation path and does not change a published milestone status.

state.reason: The systemd capability declaration adds no durable state. Default ISO storage remains in the existing Core managed journal.

verification.method: Regression first: the new Core package test failed before the declaration was added. On a disposable Debian 13 guest, the exact nex-core-local sandbox directives made runuser -u libvirt-qemu fail without CAP_SETUID and succeed with only AmbientCapabilities=CAP_SETUID added. A staged current Core service then started its embedded agent after ordinary enrollment, wrote the succeeded default ISO journal record, and a fresh Controller adopted it through Inventory.managed without manual storage registration; documented in QA. python3 -m unittest tests/test_core_local_package.py tests/test_agent_service.py tests/test_storage_packaging.py passed (24 tests).
